Tiles

Meadows: split among the packs; Scatter: placed at random
Meadows: share of the world that is meadow (most of it starts as a blade); Scatter: share of tiles that start as a blade

Meadows = meadows with open ground between

Notes: Meadows only: on = lakes and rivers settle on the ground (and beaches and thirst); off = no water anywhere and no thirst. The Debug tab's Water button overrides this for the page and starts a new world
Meters from the lowest ground to the highest (a range: each world draws its own value from it)
Tiles; how broad the ranges are that rise fastest while the ground grows (a range: each world draws its own)
0-1; how much smaller bumps ride on those ranges (a range: each world draws its own)
Lake basins pressed into the grown ground (as glaciers scoop them); water settles in them by the water rules (a range: each world draws its own)
Water on: mean mm of rain a day over the long run, on every tile (a range: each world draws its own); it falls from showers, so any one day is patchy; 0 = no water at all
km/h of the world's typical wind (a range: each world draws its own); it drifts around this, with a prevailing direction its seed picks
How many times the typical wind its strongest spells can reach; it never goes beyond
Roughly how many in-world hours the wind takes to change noticeably; its stronger spells and wandering direction are slower
Rain falls from showers: how many km across one is (each shower draws its own from the range); the wind carries it over the map
... how hard it rains under a shower, mm an hour (each shower draws its own)
... how many in-world hours a shower lasts before it is gone (each shower draws its own)
Roughly how many in-world days a wet or a dry spell lasts: the rate showers are born at wanders around its mean, slowly
How much that rate swings between wet and dry spells (the spread of its logarithm; 0 = showers come at a steady rate). Whatever it is, the long-run rain is still Rain
Lightning: share of showers that are thunderstorms (decided when a shower is born); in dry spells more of them are, up to DryStormBoost times this
Lightning: how many times StormShare the share of storms is in the driest spell (1 = dry spells make no difference)
Lightning: share of its intensity a storm's rain keeps in the driest spell (dry lightning); a wetter spell cuts it less. The world's long-run Rain is unchanged
Lightning: strikes an in-world hour from each live storm (those landing off the map are not seen)
Lightning: strikes land outside the storm's rain, in a ring from its radius out to this many times its radius
Lightning: how much more of that ring lies ahead of the storm, downwind, than behind it (0 = all round alike)
Water: in-world hours water must stand on a blade (or its tile be shore) before it drowns; water that drains off sooner leaves it alive
mm a day from standing water
mm a day plants draw from full soil, less as it dries
Meters of soil over the bedrock; 30% of it is room for water
mm a day the soil can soak up
m a day water seeps through full soil (Darcy), toward a lower water table
How easily surface water runs (1 / Manning's n): speed = this × depth^(2/3) × √slope, m/s
Days the water rules run before day 0 so a world starts settled
Rounds of lifting and river cutting that grow the ground before day 0 (more: deeper-cut valleys; slower to make)
How hard rivers cut while the ground grows (stream power)
How much slopes soften each round while the ground grows (0-0.25)
Places on the map's edge where water leaves; valleys gather into rivers that run to them (a range: each world draws its own)
Tiles; roughly how wide the largest meadows are
Meadows only: how many colonies the starting bunnies live in
Meadows only: how many packs the starting wolves run in
Meadows only: warren holes dug at each colony before its bunnies settle; Scatter has none
A new hole is dug only within this many tiles of an existing hole (unless no hole is within HoleRange)
A hole no bunny has stood on for this long collapses into bare ground
PAINT tab: days the ground at a nuke's center stays scorched (bare: nothing grows or is dug there); it shortens toward the rim so the crater greens from its edges
Fire: how fast it leaps, per in-world hour, to a full blade of bone-dry grass next to it in calm air (an in-world hour is 20/24 s at 1×); a smaller blade, damper soil or a headwind slows it
Fire: how much a strong wind tilts it (1 = a gale doubles its pace downwind and stops it upwind; 0 = wind makes no difference); a typical breeze is a third of a gale
Fire: how dry the ground is (0-100%) in a world without water; where there is water the soil's own wetness decides
Fire: days the burnt ground stays scorched (bare: nothing grows or is dug there) before grass can return
Fire: how many times faster grass grows, seeds and sprouts on a tile with ash (like CorpseBoost; where both apply, the larger counts and the other is ignored). Growth spends the ash
Fire: days for the ash on a tile to weather to half (it weathers away and never moves to another tile)
Fire: share of burnt blades whose roots live through it and resprout once the scorch is over
Fire: chance per day that living roots on burnt ground put up a new blade once the scorch is over
Fire: in-world hours a fire painted on bare ground burns (it has no fuel, so it is brief: about a second at 1×); long enough to be seen and to have a fair chance of lighting a blade beside it
PAINT tab: the default radius in tiles of the grass/rabbit/wolf/human/water brush (0 = one tile; the Radius slider overrides it per mode)
Blank = new random seed each run; the seed used is shown on screen so you can paste it here to replay that start
PAINT tab: painting past this many animals in total asks first since big crowds slow the sim down on many devices (the benchmark shows smooth to about 32000 animals on a Mac; phones vary)
